0.value:
smpl_pose_adjust adds a fixed rotation to chosen joints of an SMPL pose - for a pose that is right in shape but wrong in detail, such as a sensor that sits a little off on one limb.

WHAT IT TAKES:
An SMPL pose in AXIS-ANGLE form: three numbers per joint, at least 22 joints, flat or one row per joint. Joints past the 22nd (the hands) pass through untouched. A pose in quaternions produces no output at all - from shadow_to_smpl, set 'output_format' to axis_angle.

THE CORRECTIONS:
There is one row of three numbers per body joint, named pelvis, left_hip, and so on to right_wrist. Each row is a rotation in axis-angle form: the direction of the three numbers is the axis, and their length is the angle in radians. All zeros means no correction. A corrected joint carries everything below it with it, as a real joint would.

WHICH FRAME A CORRECTION IS IN:
The frame the rotation is applied in decides whether the correction holds as the body moves.

The pelvis correction is always in the body's own frame. Every other joint's correction is, by default, in its PARENT bone's frame. The 'child frame' checkbox switches them to the joint's OWN frame.

A sensor mounted on the child side of a joint produces an error in the child's frame, and correcting it in the parent's will drift as the joint bends. If a correction looks right in one posture and wrong in another, this is the setting.

SYNTAX:
smpl_pose_adjust

EXAMPLE:
smpl_pose_adjust

INPUTS:

pose in:
The axis-angle pose.

child frame:
Off: corrections in the parent bone's frame. On: in the joint's own frame.

reset:
Set every correction back to zero.

pelvis ... right_wrist:
The correction for each joint, as above. The values are saved with the patch and with presets.

OUTPUT:

pose out:
The corrected pose, one row per joint. Joints without a correction come out exactly as they went in.

RELATED:
smpl_mag_yaw_correct corrects magnetometer heading errors joint by joint. floor_zero puts the feet on the floor.
